text: Git is a version control system that helps developers manage changes to their code. One of its most useful features is branching. A branch lets you work on new ideas without affecting the main code. For example, you can create a feature branch to build a new function safely. When your work is ready, you merge the branch back into the main project. Teams often use pull requests to review changes before merging. This workflow keeps the code organized and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merges, and pull requests together, developers can collaborate smoothly and keep their projects stable.
